summary: Both paragraphs are close to the Hebrew and keep the ruled terms, but 1:6 has real faults. In 1:5 several words were dropped (הספר, a second 'this is', ס' of the Zohar, על of עובר על) and 'Ri'f' departs from the ruled 'the Rif'. In 1:6 the clause about the early students misreads לרשב״י as 'he was', ל״ג is rendered 32 against the wave 1 ruling, the nested quotation marks are broken, and 'he scraped their join' and 'on one parchment' misread שקלף and בעור. The Num 15:39, Deut 16:19 and Prov 23:31 verses were missed or not identified, and the notes on 1:6.171, 1:6.185 and 1:6.305 are false.

patches.value: And I named the book The Wars of the LORD for His unity, because the philosopher, the author of the book the Zohar, spoiled for us the truth of the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, and several rabbis and great men of the Torah followed him with eyes shut. And of them Solomon said in his wisdom: "For she has cast down many slain, and mighty are all her slain." As our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin, the Rif): "For she has cast down many slain" this is a student who has not reached instruction and teaches, (as we see with our own eyes how many authors who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle, from the scantness of their expertise) "and mighty are all her slain" this is a student who has reached instruction and does not teach (who does not set his mind to teach others correctly; "mighty" is the word of "and he shuts his eyes", Rashi of blessed memory). And all the more so, if he entices others to occupy themselves with the external book, the book of the Zohar, and does not set his mind to understand the contradiction, but walks with the eye of reason shut, and makes others stumble in a false faith, of whom it is said, "and mighty are all her slain"; and transgresses against "and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block"; and error in study counts as wilful sin, and he sins and causes the many to sin, and the sin of the many hangs on him.
patches.reason: Fidelity and decisions. (1) הספר in מחבר הספר הזהר was dropped: 'the author of the book the Zohar'. (2) 'Sanhedrin, [in] the Rif' is the ruled form, not 'Ri'f'. (3) The second 'this is' (זה, 1:5.67) was left out; the first exposition has it. (4) ס' הזהר, 'the book of the Zohar', lost its ס'. (5) עובר על: the preposition על was left unrendered and glossed '(governs the verb above)', and the cited Lev 19:14 was left running on as if a clause of the author. (6) נותן לב is an idiom: translated by its sense (checklist and Talmudic idiom rule), not 'give heart'.

patches.value: הספר: 'the book'. The decisions fix 'the author of the Zohar' for מחבר הזהר; here the Hebrew has מחבר הספר הזהר, so the English keeps 'the book': 'the author of the book the Zohar'.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent on the longer form מחבר הספר הזהר. Proposed ruling: keep every word, 'the author of the book the Zohar', and keep 'the author of the Zohar' only for מחבר הזהר.
Ruling (wave 1): 'Sanhedrin, [in] the Rif', as written.

patches.value: רי״ף: the Rif (Rabbi Yitzchak Alfasi); the reference is kept as the author writes it, 'Sanhedrin, the Rif', with no volume or folio added.
patches.reason: The note named the old spelling 'Ri'f' and did not say who is meant (decisions: say in a note who is meant).
נותן לב is an idiom ('gives heart'), 'sets his mind'.

patches.value: נותן לב: idiom, literally 'gives heart': to pay attention, to set one's mind to something.
patches.reason: A learner needs the literal sense of the idiom.
Same idiom as 1:5.74.

patches.value: נותן לב: the same idiom, 'gives heart': to set one's mind to understanding the contradiction.

patches.value: Rashi (quoted by the author at 1:5.83) connects ועצומים with the verb עוצם, 'he shuts': so 'mighty' is glossed 'he shuts his eyes', which echoes 'with eyes shut' (1:5.25-26) and 'the eye of reason shut' (1:5.102-104).
patches.reason: The old note said the gloss came 'earlier in the paragraph'. The gloss is the words that follow, in 1:5.80-82, and the old note is confused.

patches.value: בספ׳ is the abbreviation of בספר, 'in the book of'; here the sense is 'in the book'.
patches.reason: Abbreviations are named in a token note (decisions).
ס׳ is ספר, 'book of', construct before הזהר; the gloss 'the book' lost the construct.

patches.value: ס׳ is the abbreviation of ספר.
patches.reason: Abbreviations are named in a token note (decisions).
על is 'against' in עובר על; '(governs the verb above)' is not a gloss and the word was left unrendered.

patches.value: עובר על: 'transgresses against'. על takes the cited prohibition that follows, Lev 19:14 (ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול).
patches.reason: A learner needs the construction.

value: וקראתי is a perfect with waw ('and I called'); with שם הספר it means 'named the book'.
The reason clause runs from כי (1:5.8) to בעצימת עינים (1:5.25-26): the philosopher spoiled the truth of the unity, and the followers went after him with eyes shut. From ועליהם a new sentence begins.
כי רבים חללים הפילה is Prov 7:26, said of the 'strange woman' of Prov 7 and here applied to the author of the Zohar; הפילה is a perfect, third feminine singular.
Each זה ('this is') in the Talmudic exposition introduces a rabbinic identification of one of the verse's words; the English keeps 'this is' at each point.
דמעיילי פילא בקופא דמחטא is a Talmudic Aramaic idiom for doing the impossible; the English gives its sense, 'who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle'.
ועובר על takes the cited prohibition, Lev 19:14, as its object; ושגגת תלמוד עולה זדון is a rabbinic maxim cited without a formula.
patches.reason: The old second note said the reason clause ran to the end of the paragraph. It ends at 1:5.26. The old list also left the Aramaic idiom and the על construction unexplained.

value: The text is the Wikisource base text; Wikisource additions and corrections are not flagged word by word until the 1931 scan is collated (decisions, Q2).
The title: מלחמות ה׳ takes the form of Num 21:14, 'ספר מלחמת ה׳' (the book of the Wars of the LORD).
Prov 7:26, quoted: 'For she has cast down many slain, and mighty are all her slain' (translated from the verse as he quotes it).
Lev 19:14, 'ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול', cited after 'ועובר על': 'and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block'.
'Sanhedrin' and 'the Rif' as written; the Talmudic gloss on the verse is his paraphrase and is not marked as a quotation.
patches.reason: The decisions require a general Wikisource line on the unit's first segment (Q2), which was missing. The Num 21:14 source of the title was not given, and the Lev 19:14 line said 'no quotation marks' although the verse is the object of עובר על.

patches.value: And concerning this external faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Yalkut, Parashat Kedoshim, and the Midrash ha-Gadol there, and the Rambam in Sefer ha-Mitzvot, negative commandment 10): "Do not turn to the idols, and the gods of; if you turn to others (to honor them, Sforno), your end is to make them divinities." Thus far. And so it befell the faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, for the early students who learned from it, thinking that it was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's, they thought to make sense of his words; and to call the partzufim vessels, and they esteemed them and honored them, and those who came after them made them divinities, according to the thought of the philosopher, the author, and accepted them upon themselves as divinities, as will be explained within. And likewise our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded in the verse: wine and strong drink you shall not drink, and these are his words: "Rabbi Chiya opened: 'The precepts of the LORD are right'; and it is written of wine: 'it goes down smoothly'; and it is written: 'rejoicing the heart'; and it is written: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man.' Just as this wine gladdens the heart, so the words of Torah gladden the heart; just as this wine, one who drinks of it more than his need in the end vomits everything; so the words of Torah, one who occupies himself with them and thinks about them too much, in the end he goes out into heresy." Thus far. (Midrash ha-Gadol, Parashat Shemini, verse 'wine and strong drink'). In this way did the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, act, to follow after his heart, to think about the words of Torah too much, in paths far from the truth, and very far from the rules that the Sages received, a man from the mouth of a man, by which the Torah is expounded, and these are the thirteen rules of Rabbi Ishmael and the thirty-three rules of Rabbi Yose the Galilean, for the Aggadah, as the discerning, attentive reader will see; and he enticed and seduced the sages, the upright of heart, who walk in their simplicity, to believe him in his lies: that there was revealed to him the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him the Elder of Elders, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and Elijah, and they revealed to him secrets of heresy, which it is forbidden to think about them, even in the lavatory; and he promised one who occupies himself with his Torah without understanding, a reward greater than the essentials of the Torah, in order to blind the eyes of the sages and to stop up the way of study in his words so as not to understand his machinations, and to magnify the merit of those who occupy themselves with his new Torah, full of idols different in their essences and their activities, without being particular about the addition and multiplicity, in our God, the Unique, above all other ones; and do not take note how the Torah was strict about 'you shall not add', whether in tefillin, or in a mezuzah, or in the four species of the lulav, and likewise in the other commandments, even though he puts five sections in one hide and he joins them to be one, and likewise, if he adds one section to a mezuzah, even though parchment joins them to be one, we do not say 'as though it were not one'; and likewise in tzitzit, and in the bundle of four species, if he added a fifth species to the bundle, it is disqualified; and we do not say 'as though it were not one'.
patches.reason: Fidelity and decisions. (1) בחשבם שהוא לרשב״י התנא: ל is possessive; the students thought the BOOK was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's, not that 'he' (the author) was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; the old English also says something the Hebrew does not. (2) ול״ג מדות is 'thirty-three' as written (wave 1 ruling; the old English and note applied the superseded 32). (3) The nested quotation marks were broken (an unclosed single quote) and ביין was folded into the quotation. (4) 'that he goes out' is no sentence; 'In this way did ... to search' has no main verb (checklist 1), and לתור אחרי לבבו is Num 15:39, 'to follow after his heart'. (5) איש מפי איש lost מפי. (6) להאמינו lost the pronoun. (7) הנקרא is passive (checklist 4). (8) גופי תורה is 'the essentials of the Torah' ('bodies of'), not 'plain text'. (9) בל תוסיף is the name of the prohibition, quoted: 'the prohibition' was an added word. (10) בעור אחד is 'in one hide' (עור was unrendered, glossed 'on'); שקלף is ש + קלף 'that parchment' joining the sections, not 'he scraped their join' (invented word); להיות is 'to be', not 'to make'. (11) The Hebrew has one full stop; the English had stray full stops and a capital 'And' / lower-case 'and' after a stop. (12) The idiom נותן לב and the verb חשב are rendered consistently by sense. (13) '(Sforno: to honor them)' reordered the author's gloss.

ואלהי is construct ('gods of'), and in Lev 19:4 it continues 'מסכה'. The author's quotation breaks off. Proposed ruling: translate the construct as written, 'and the gods of', add nothing, and say in a note that the quotation is cut short.

patches.value: ואלהי: construct state, 'gods of'. Lev 19:4 reads 'ואלהי מסכה'; the author's wording is cut off after ואלהי and followed by his own words, which are translated as he gives them.
patches.reason: The old note called the wording 'followed as he gives it' but the English had dropped the construct.
שהוא refers to the book (הזהר), not to a person.
לרשב״י has the possessive ל.

patches.value: רשב״י is written out in full (decisions). ל־ is possessive: the early students thought the book was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's. The English does not say more than the Hebrew about who wrote it.
patches.reason: A learner needs the construction; the decisions keep the two figures apart.
Apposition to the possessive of 1:6.51.
יתהלך is a verb (yiqtol, 'it goes'); the old gloss had no subject and ביין (1:6.93) is 'of wine'.
ומחשב is the verb חשב, rendered 'think' consistently (also 1:6.159, 1:6.221).
לתור אחרי לבבו alludes to Num 15:39 (ולא תתורו אחרי לבבכם): 'to follow after the heart'.

patches.value: לתור אחרי לבבו alludes to Num 15:39, ולא תתורו אחרי לבבכם, 'and you shall not follow after your heart'.
patches.reason: The allusion must be recognised (decisions: Bible verses).
Consistent rendering of חשב.
ב after חשב is 'about'.

patches.value: Literally 'measures' (המדות); the hermeneutical rules by which the Torah is expounded, as the next clauses show (the thirteen rules of Rabbi Ishmael and the rules of Rabbi Yose the Galilean).
patches.reason: The old note sent the learner to a use 'in 1:5' where the word does not occur.
Wave 1 ruling: translate the number as written (ל״ג is 33).

patches.value: ל״ג is the letters for thirty-three, as written. The tradition counts thirty-two rules of Rabbi Yose the Galilean.
patches.reason: The old note says the work renders thirty-two; the wave 1 ruling overrides that entry.
Consistent rendering of חשב.
גופי תורה is an idiom (literally 'bodies of Torah'): the main substance of the Torah, not its 'plain text'. Proposed ruling: 'the essentials of the Torah', literal 'bodies' in the token note.

patches.value: מגופי תורה: literally 'than the bodies of Torah'; גופי תורה are the essentials, the main body of the Torah's law.
patches.reason: A learner needs the literal sense of the idiom.
שונים is 'different, differing' (in essences and activities).
ולא יתנו לב: idiom, 'take note'.
בל תוסיף is quoted by its words; the gloss 'the prohibition' added a word.

patches.value: בל תוסיף: 'you shall not add', the rabbinic name of the prohibition against adding to the commandments (Deut 4:2, 13:1), quoted by its words.
patches.reason: A learner needs the name; the verse goes in apparatus.
בעור is 'in hide / leather'; 'on' is the wrong preposition and עור was not rendered anywhere.
להיות is 'to be', not 'to make'.
שקלף is ש + קלף, the noun 'parchment', subject of מחברן; compare the tefillin case, 'in one hide ... joins them'. 'He scraped' leaves מחברן without sense and invents 'their join'.

patches.value: שקלף: ש + קלף, 'that parchment'. The sections are joined into one piece by the parchment, as in the tefillin case above (בעור אחד).
patches.reason: The old note gave the verb reading 'scraped', which the sentence does not support.
מחברן is the participle 'joins them', not 'their join'.
לחיות is a spelling of להיות.

patches.value: לחיות: the spelling in the witness for להיות, 'to be'; translated as the evident word and recorded in apparatus.
patches.reason: Decisions: variant spellings are recorded.

patches.value: כלא חד: Aramaic, the author's halakhic formula. Rendered 'as though it were not one' (the same ruling as 1:7, which the owner will review); a possible alternative is כולא חד, 'it is all one'.
patches.reason: The owner holds ולא אמרינן כלא חד for 1:7. The same words occur twice here (1:6.309-312, 1:6.324-327). Proposed ruling: the same English in all three places and the alternative kept in apparatus until the owner decides.

value: The paragraph is one long period. The quotation from Lev 19:4 (in the Yalkut, Midrash ha-Gadol and Rambam) runs from 'Do not turn' to 'Thus far'; its parenthesis is Sforno's gloss, kept in parentheses.

The Midrash ha-Gadol passage (Rabbinic Hebrew) chains verses with 'and it is written' (וכתיב): Ps 19:9, Prov 23:31 (in the Midrash's wording) and Ps 104:15. Its analogy 'just as ... so' (מה ... כך) carries the argument, and the second half turns on 'too much' (מדאי).
The infinitives after עשה (לתור, לחשב, להעור, ולסתום, ולהגדיל) give the purpose of the philosopher's deed; לתור אחרי לבבו alludes to Num 15:39, and להעור עיני חכמים to Deut 16:19.
בחשבם שהוא לרשב״י התנא: the ל of לרשב״י is possessive. The early students thought the book was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's.
The verbs in the sentence about the early students (חשבו, והחשיבום, וכיבדו, עשו, וקיבלום) narrate what followed from the first error, in the perfect with waw.
דאגדתא, מינין and לא אמרינן כלא חד are Talmudic Aramaic inside the author's Hebrew; the last two clauses are the halakhic conclusion of the paragraph and the English keeps them as parallel sentences.
patches.reason: The old list left the possessive ל of לרשב״י unexplained, omitted Prov 23:31 from the chain of verses, and did not label the Aramaic.

value: Lev 19:4, quoted words 'Do not turn to the idols' (אל תפנו אל האלילים). The rest of the quotation is the author's wording (ואלהי אם אתה פונה אחרים) and is rendered as he gives it; in the verse ואלהי continues 'מסכה'.
Lev 10:9, 'Wine and strong drink you shall not drink' (in the verse: wine and strong drink).
Ps 19:9: 'The precepts of the LORD are right' and 'rejoicing the heart' (משמחי לב).
Prov 23:31: 'ביין יתהלך במישרים' ('of wine: it goes down smoothly'); the verse has 'כי יתן בכוס עינו יתהלך במישרים' and the Midrash's wording is rendered as he gives it.
Ps 104:15: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man' (ויין ישמח לבב אנוש).
Num 15:39, alluded to in 'לתור אחרי לבבו' (to follow after his heart).
Deut 16:19, alluded to in 'להעור עיני חכמים' (a bribe 'blinds the eyes of the wise').
'בל תוסיף', the rabbinic name of the prohibition of Deut 4:2 and 13:1 (לא תספו / לא תסף עליו).
ל״ג in 'ול״ג מדות דר׳ יוסי הגלילי' is written as thirty-three by letters; the English follows the wave 1 ruling (thirty-three). The usual count of Rabbi Yose the Galilean's rules is thirty-two.
לחיות (1:6.307) is the witness's spelling of להיות; translated 'to be'.
כלא חד (1:6.311, 1:6.326): rendered 'as though it were not one' under the owner's reservation on 1:7; a possible alternative reading is כולא חד, 'it is all one'.
patches.reason: The old list identified Prov 23:31 as 'not identified', followed the superseded 32, and did not give Deut 16:19, the source of בל תוסיף, the spelling לחיות or the כלא חד reservation.
